newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols pumped up pre-payrolls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. T-bond vols pumped up pre-payrolls.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were pumped up in late trade ahead of Friday's February employment report, dealers said.
A gradual slide in underlying bond prices from early highs was also indicative of the market's heightened concerns about a near-term Federal Reserve credit tightening, they added.

"There was a lot of put buying, basically setting up for tomorrow's number," said a brokerage trader at the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT). "I think most people think the propensity is to the downside."
April puts, which expire in about two weeks, were particularly well bid. Short-dated options have higher gamma and therefore have quicker premium acceleration when underlying prices swing.
Implied volatility for CBOT April T-bond futures options had risen to around 10.7 percent by mid-afternoon from Wednesday's 10.3 close. June was up 0.1-0.2 point to 10.0.

While some traders doubted the Fed would raise interest rates at its March 25 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, most agreed that the market was accepting a tightening by May or July to be inevitable.
